_note: The ability modifier for every legal score, 1 to 30 — the arithmetic every
other rule on the sheet is built on. Go has it in internal/http/forge.go,
TypeScript in lib/abilities.ts, and neither may move without this file
These numbers are copied from the SRD table, not generated from either
implementation, so the fixture is an independent answer rather than a
record of what the code already does.
The odd scores below 10 are the whole reason this exists. The rule is
floor((score - 10) / 2), and Go's integer division truncates toward zero
instead — so the obvious transcription gives 0 for a score of 9 where the
table says -1, and is wrong for every odd score under 10. forge.go carries
an explicit correction for it; this is what stops that correction being
tidied away by someone who reads it as a rounding preference.
